mission: SINGLE CANARY #3 - an overbroad inventory span must not discharge semantics it does not represent. No other audit defect addressed.

fixture.source: The Borrower shall not incur Indebtedness exceeding $10,000,000. The Borrower shall maintain a Leverage Ratio of not more than 4.00 to 1.00 as of the last day of each fiscal quarter. The cure period is 30 days.
fixture.inventory: ONE item, materiality CRITICAL, role OTHER, span 0-210 (the whole region), proposition "this section contains provisions"

before.coverageSpans: one COVERED_BY_INVENTORY span over the entire region

fixture.note: the item's three quantitative values are auto-attached by Pass A normalisation, so an IR carrying MONEY 10000000, RATIO 4 and a condition naming 30 days reconciles it REPRESENTED - exactly the audit's harness

earliestResponsibleBranch: computeSourceCoverage's mask fill in lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-accountability/source-coverage.ts - `mask.fill(1, s.charStart, s.charEnd)`
rootCause: Raw character overlap was treated as semantic coverage. A span is evidence about the ONE proposition its item represents; the mask made it evidence about everything inside the same character range, and once filled nothing downstream could tell the difference. Every later layer - unaccounted spans, unaccounted values, reconciliation, completeness - inherited that conflation.

ruleChosen.name: coverage credit is clipped to the independent structural segment the span STARTS in (mission §5 option C, with §5 option D's provenance split)
ruleChosen.independentBoundary: a clause terminator (. ; : ! ?) followed by whitespace, or a line break - deliberately NARROWER than the unit segmenter, which also splits at commas, dashes and enumerators because those separate the PARTS of one proposition, not one proposition from the next
ruleChosen.provenancePreserved: the item keeps its full source span in the frozen inventory; only coverage CREDIT is clipped
ruleChosen.conservativeDefault: an item spanning 'Clause A. Clause B. Clause C.' credits A only; B and C stay accountable because there is no deterministic basis for believing the item represents them
whatItIsNot: no attempt to interpret legal prose or compare proposition text to source

productionFilesChanged: lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-accountability/source-coverage.ts (independentSegmentBounds, clipCreditToStartSegment, applied at the mask fill)
